claim: CRISPR/Cas9 efficiently induces targeted mutations via non-homologous-end-joining.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 efficiently induces targeted mutations via non-homologous-end-joining but for genome editing, precise, homology-directed repair (HDR) of endogenous DNA stretches is a prerequisite.
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field of genome editing, supported by extensive literature.

claim: Precise, homology-directed repair (HDR) of endogenous DNA stretches is a prerequisite for genome editing.
source: CRISPR/Cas9 efficiently induces targeted mutations via non-homologous-end-joining but for genome editing, precise, homology-directed repair (HDR) of endogenous DNA stretches is a prerequisite.
evidence: This represents a fundamental requirement in the field based on established understanding of genome editing mechanisms.

claim: Modification of 5' ends of long dsDNA donors strongly enhances HDR in Medaka.
source: Using Medaka we show that the modification of 5' ends of long dsDNA donors strongly enhances HDR, favors efficient single-copy integration by retaining a monomeric donor conformation thus facilitating successful gene replacement or tagging.
evidence: This is the primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data presented in the manuscript including Southern blots and PCR genotyping.

claim: 5' modification of long dsDNA donors favors efficient single-copy integration by retaining a monomeric donor conformation.
source: Using Medaka we show that the modification of 5' ends of long dsDNA donors strongly enhances HDR, favors efficient single-copy integration by retaining a monomeric donor conformation thus facilitating successful gene replacement or tagging.
evidence: This claim is supported by Southern blot data showing monomeric state of modified donors and PCR genotyping showing single-copy integration.

claim: The implementation of the bacterial CRISPR/Cas9 system in eukaryotes has triggered a quantum leap in targeted genome editing in literally any organism with a sequenced genome or targeting region.
source: The implementation of the bacterial CRISPR/Cas9 system in eukaryotes has triggered a quantum leap in targeted genome editing in literally any organism with a sequenced genome or targeting region (Cong et al., 2013; Jinek et al., 2012; Mali et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to foundational CRISPR/Cas9 papers.

claim: Site-specific double-strand breaks (DSBs) are catalyzed by the Cas9 enzyme guided by a single RNA with a short complementary region to the target site.
source: Site-specific double-strand breaks (DSBs) are catalyzed by the Cas9 enzyme guided by a single RNA with a short complementary region to the target site.
evidence: This describes the established mechanism of CRISPR/Cas9 action.

claim: The endogenous non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) DNA repair machinery seals the DSB in response to Cas9-induced breaks.
source: In response, the endogenous non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) DNA repair machinery seals the DSB.
evidence: This is a well-established cellular response to double-strand breaks.

claim: Perfect repair will restore the CRISPR/Cas9 target site.
source: Since perfect repair will restore the CRISPR/Cas9 target site, mutations introduced by imprecise NHEJ are selected for.
evidence: This is a logical consequence of the repair mechanism and target site recognition.

claim: Mutations introduced by imprecise NHEJ are selected for.
source: Since perfect repair will restore the CRISPR/Cas9 target site, mutations introduced by imprecise NHEJ are selected for.
evidence: This is inferred from the mechanism where perfect repair restores the target site, allowing repeated cutting.

claim: HDR is preferentially active during the late S/G2 phase of the cell cycle.
source: To acquire precise genome editing the initial DSB should be fixed via the homology-directed repair (HDR) mechanism which is preferentially active during the late S/G2 phase of the cell cycle (Hustedt and Durocher, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hustedt and Durocher, 2017.

claim: Donor DNA templates with flanking regions homologous to the target locus are used to introduce specific mutations or particular DNA sequences.
source: Donor DNA templates with flanking regions homologous to the target locus are used to introduce specific mutations or particular DNA sequences.
evidence: This describes the standard approach for HDR-mediated genome editing.

claim: Injected (linear) dsDNA rapidly multimerizes.
source: Injected (linear) dsDNA rapidly multimerizes (Winkler et al., 1991), which likely also happens in CRISPR/Cas9 based approaches.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Winkler et al., 1991.

claim: Multimerization of injected linear dsDNA likely also happens in CRISPR/Cas9 based approaches.
source: Injected (linear) dsDNA rapidly multimerizes (Winkler et al., 1991), which likely also happens in CRISPR/Cas9 based approaches.
evidence: This is an inference based on the cited behavior of injected DNA.

claim: The high activity of NHEJ re-ligating CRISPR/Cas9 mediated DSBs can multimerize injected (linear) dsDNA donor templates.
source: Additionally, the high activity of NHEJ re-ligating CRISPR/Cas9 mediated DSBs can multimerize injected (linear) dsDNA donor templates.
evidence: This is inferred from the known activity of NHEJ and its potential to ligate DNA ends.

claim: Precise HDR-mediated recombination of single-copy donor templates is rather rare.
source: This poses a problem since consequently, the precise HDR-mediated recombination of single-copy donor templates is rather rare.
evidence: This is inferred from the multimerization problem described in the preceding sentences.

claim: NHEJ was interfered with by pharmacological inhibition of DNA ligase IV.
source: NHEJ was interfered with by pharmacological inhibition of DNA ligase IV (Maruyama et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Maruyama et al., 2015.

claim: HDR was meant to be favored by fusing the HDR-mediating yeast protein Rad52 to Cas9.
source: Conversely, HDR was meant to be favored by fusing the HDR-mediating yeast protein Rad52 to Cas9 (Wang et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Wang et al., 2017.

claim: Removal of Cas9 in the G1/S phase by linking it to the N-terminal region of the DNA replication inhibitor Geminin should restrict the introduction of double-strand cuts to the G2 phase.
source: Similarly, removal of Cas9 in the G1/S phase (Gutschner et al., 2016) by linking it to the N-terminal region of the DNA replication inhibitor Geminin, should restrict the introduction of double-strand cuts to the G2 phase, when HDR is most prominently occurring (Hustedt and Durocher, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Gutschner et al., 2016 and Hustedt and Durocher, 2017.

claim: HDR is most prominently occurring in the G2 phase.
source: Similarly, removal of Cas9 in the G1/S phase (Gutschner et al., 2016) by linking it to the N-terminal region of the DNA replication inhibitor Geminin, should restrict the introduction of double-strand cuts to the G2 phase, when HDR is most prominently occurring (Hustedt and Durocher, 2017).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Hustedt and Durocher, 2017.

claim: Previous approaches improved HDR-mediated integration of the homology flanks, while they did not tackle reported integration of multimers.
source: Those approaches improved HDR-mediated integration of the homology flanks, while they did not tackle reported integration of multimers (Auer et al., 2014) arising after injection of dsDNA templates such as plasmids or PCR products (Winkler et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Auer et al., 2014 and Winkler et al., 1991.

claim: Integration of multimers arises after injection of dsDNA templates such as plasmids or PCR products.
source: Those approaches improved HDR-mediated integration of the homology flanks, while they did not tackle reported integration of multimers (Auer et al., 2014) arising after injection of dsDNA templates such as plasmids or PCR products (Winkler et al., 1991).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Auer et al., 2014 and Winkler et al., 1991.

claim: Blocking both 5´ends of PCR amplified long dsDNA donor cassettes using 'bulky' moieties like Biotin, Amino-dT and carbon spacers should shield the DNA donor from multimerization and integration via NHEJ.
source: We thus blocked both 5´ends of PCR amplified long dsDNA donor cassettes using 'bulky' moieties like Biotin, Amino-dT (A-dT) and carbon spacers (e. g. Spacer C3, SpC3). This should shield the DNA donor from multimerization and integration via NHEJ, thus favoring precise and efficient single-copy integration via HDR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is the hypothesis being tested in the study, with supporting data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: 5' modification with bulky moieties should favor precise and efficient single-copy integration via HDR.
source: We thus blocked both 5´ends of PCR amplified long dsDNA donor cassettes using 'bulky' moieties like Biotin, Amino-dT (A-dT) and carbon spacers (e. g. Spacer C3, SpC3). This should shield the DNA donor from multimerization and integration via NHEJ, thus favoring precise and efficient single-copy integration via HDR (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is the hypothesis being tested, with experimental validation shown in subsequent figures.

claim: dsDNA donors established by A-dT modified primers multimerized and produced similar results as unmodified DIG-labelled dsDNA donors.
source: dsDNA donors established by A-dT modified primes, however, multimerized and produced similar results as unmodified DIG-labelled dsDNA donors (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by Southern blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: In unmodified DIG-labelled control donors, multimerization was uncovered already at 2 hr post-injection as evident by a ladder of labeled donor DNA representing different copy number multimers.
source: In unmodified DIG-labelled control donors, we uncovered multimerization already at 2 hr post-injection as evident by a ladder of labeled donor DNA representing different copy number multimers (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the Southern blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Biotin and SpC3 modification of DIG-labelled donors prevented multimerization within six hours post-injection.
source: In contrast, Biotin and SpC3 modification of DIG-labelled donors prevented multimerization within six hours post-injection (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the Southern blot data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The 5' modification of dsDNA did not apparently enhance the stability of the resulting dsDNA.
source: While strongly blocking multimerization, the 5' modification of dsDNA did not apparently enhance the stability of the resulting dsDNA (compare modified and unmodified donors over time, Figure 1B).
evidence: This is observed by comparing the signal intensity over time in Figure 1B.

claim: For all four loci tested, efficient targeting was observed as apparent by the GFP expression within the expected expression domain.
source: For all four loci (and all 5' modifications) tested we observed efficient targeting as apparent by the GFP expression within the expected expression domain (Figure 2A, Supplementary file 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by GFP expression data shown in Figure 2A and supplementary files.

claim: The survival rates of embryos injected with Biotin and SpC3 5' modified dsDNA donors did not differ significantly from embryos injected with the unmodified dsDNA control donors.
source: The survival rates of embryos injected with Biotin and SpC3 5' modified dsDNA donors did not differ significantly from embryos injected with the unmodified dsDNA control donors (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Supplementary file 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: The injection of the A-dT 5' modified dsDNA donors resulted in high embryonic lethality.
source: In contrast, the injection of the A-dT 5' modified dsDNA donors resulted in high embryonic lethality (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by survival data shown in Supplementary file 1 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1.

claim: Employing unmodified donors, the rate of HDR was very low as evidenced by the predominant amplification of the alleles without gfp integration.
source: Employing unmodified donors, the rate of HDR was very low as evidenced by the predominant amplification of the alleles without gfp integration (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by PCR genotyping data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The 5' modified long dsDNA donors resulted in efficient HDR already detectable in the injected generation for all targeted loci.
source: In strong contrast, the 5' modified long dsDNA donors resulted in efficient HDR already detectable in the injected generation for all targeted loci.
evidence: This is supported by PCR genotyping and sequencing data shown in multiple figures.

claim: For the gfp tagging of rx2, 6 out of 10 randomly selected, GFP-expressing embryos showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration in F0.
source: For the gfp tagging of rx2, 6 out of 10 randomly selected, GFP-expressing embryos showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration in F0 (Figure 2—figure supplement 2) as sequence confirmed by the analysis of the locus (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by PCR genotyping and sequencing data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2 and 3.

claim: 9.5% of injected and surviving zygotes showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration for rx2.
source: Thus, 9.5% of injected and surviving zygotes showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration (15.8% of the injected zygotes expressed GFP; 60% of those showed the precise single-copy integration; Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is calculated from the experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: For the gfp tagging of actb, 46.5% of the injected zygotes expressed GFP.
source: For the gfp tagging of actb 46.5% of the injected zygotes expressed GFP, 35% of which (7 out of 20 randomly selected, GFP-expressing embryos) showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration in F0, accounting for 16.3% of the initially injected zygotes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is from experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: For actb, 35% of GFP-expressing embryos showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration in F0, accounting for 16.3% of the initially injected zygotes.
source: For the gfp tagging of actb 46.5% of the injected zygotes expressed GFP, 35% of which (7 out of 20 randomly selected, GFP-expressing embryos) showed precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration in F0, accounting for 16.3% of the initially injected zygotes (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is calculated from experimental data presented in Supplementary file 1.

claim: In the case of dnmt1, all GFP-expressing embryos showed the desired perfect integration.
source: In the case of dnmt1, the rate of precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration was even higher, since full gene functionality is required for the progression of development and embryonic survival. Here, strikingly, all GFP-expressing embryo showed the desired perfect integration.
evidence: This is supported by PCR genotyping data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: For dnmt1, full gene functionality is required for the progression of development and embryonic survival.
source: In the case of dnmt1, the rate of precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration was even higher, since full gene functionality is required for the progression of development and embryonic survival.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that all GFP-expressing embryos showed perfect integration, suggesting selection for functional alleles.

claim: The highest efficiency of HDR targeting by 5' modified dsDNA for all loci tested was observed for 5'Biotin modified donors.
source: We observed the highest efficiency of HDR targeting by 5' modified dsDNA for all loci tested for 5'Biotin modified donors (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by comparative PCR genotyping data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: SpC3 5' modified dsDNA donors resulted in elevated levels of additional bands indicative for the integration of higher order multimers and NHEJ events.
source: While still giving rise to a high percentage of HDR events, SpC3 5' modified dsDNA donors also resulted in elevated levels of additional bands indicative for the integration of higher order multimers and NHEJ events (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is observed in the PCR genotyping data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: The use of RNPs (Cas9 protein and respective sgRNA) did not get close to the efficiency achieved by co-injection of Cas9 mRNA and the corresponding sgRNA.
source: Even though increasingly popular, in our hands the use of RNPs (Cas9 protein and respective sgRNA) did not even get close to the efficiency achieved by co-injection of Cas9 mRNA and the corresponding sgRNA assessed by gene targeting as described above.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experimental observations comparing the two methods.

claim: The precise integration detected in the injected generation was successfully transmitted to the next generation.
source: The precise integration detected in the injected generation was successfully transmitted to the next generation (Figure 3, Figure 2—figure supplement 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by genotyping and sequencing data from F1 and F2 generations shown in the referenced figures.

claim: For gfp-rx2, 9% of fish originating from the initially injected embryos successfully transmitted the precisely modified locus to the next generation.
source: For gfp-rx2, 9% of fish originating from the initially injected embryos successfully transmitted the precisely modified locus to the next generation (15.8% of the injected embryos expressed GFP; 4 out of 7 GFP transmitting founder fish were also transmitting the precise single integration of the gfp donor cassette).
evidence: This is calculated from germline transmission data.

claim: For gfp-rx1, 3.9% of fish originating from the initially injected embryos were transmitting the precise single copy integrate to the next generation.
source: For gfp-rx1, 3.9% of fish originating from the initially injected embryos were transmitting the precise single copy integrate to the next generation (13.5% of injected embryos expressed GFP; 2 out of 7 GFP transmitting founder fish were also transmitting the precise single integration of the gfp-rx1 donor cassette).
evidence: This is calculated from germline transmission data.

claim: For dnmt1, the high rate of precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration observed in the injected generation was fully maintained in the transmission to the next generation due to the absolute requirement of a functional/functionally tagged version of the locus.
source: For dnmt1, the high rate of precise HDR-mediated single-copy integration observed in the injected generation was fully maintained in the transmission to the next generation due to the absolute requirement of a functional/functionally tagged version of the locus.
evidence: This is inferred from the essential nature of dnmt1 and the observation of consistent perfect integration.

claim: The precise integration of the gfp donor cassette into the actb locus results in late embryonic lethality.
source: As we found in the course of our study, the precise integration of the gfp donor cassette into the actb locus results in late embryonic lethality.
evidence: This is an observation made during the study.

claim: Stable transgenic lines for actb could not be established due to late embryonic lethality.
source: As we found in the course of our study, the precise integration of the gfp donor cassette into the actb locus results in late embryonic lethality. Consequently, stable transgenic lines could not be established.
evidence: This is a direct consequence of the observed lethality.

claim: For gfp-rx2, the germline transmission rate ranged from 0.8% up to 12.9% indicating an HDR event earliest at the 4-cell stage.
source: For gfp-rx2, this rate ranged from 0.8% up to 12.9% indicating an HDR event earliest at the 4-cell stage (assuming that only a single event occurred per blastomere).
evidence: This is inferred from the germline transmission rates observed.

claim: For gfp-rx1, HDR did not occur at the one-cell stage but rather later (2–8 cell stage as reflected by germline transmission rates of 23.9% and 5.8% respectively).
source: In the case of gfp-rx1, HDR did not occur at the one-cell stage but rather later (2–8 cell stage as reflected by germline transmission rates of 23.9% and 5.8% respectively).
evidence: This is inferred from the germline transmission rates observed.

claim: For both rx2 and rx1, the transmission rates of the perfectly tagged locus reflect a level of mosaicism indicative for an HDR event between the 4- and 32-cell stage.
source: Thus, for both cases, the transmission rates of the perfectly tagged locus reflect a level of mosaicism indicative for an HDR event between the 4- and 32-cell stage.
evidence: This is inferred from the germline transmission data.

claim: Southern Blot analysis of F2 gfp-rx2 embryos reveals a single band for digestion schemes, indicating precise single-copy donor integration.
source: Southern Blot analysis of F2 gfp-rx2 embryos reveals a single band for a digestion scheme cutting outside the donor cassette (BglII/HindIII) or within the 5' donor cassette and in intron 2 (ScaI/HindIII) indicating precise single-copy donor integration.
evidence: This is directly observed in the Southern blot data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Southern Blot analysis of F2 gfp-rx1 embryos reveals a single band for digestion schemes, indicating precise single-copy donor integration.
source: Southern Blot analysis of F2 gfp-rx1 embryos reveals a single band for a digestion scheme cutting outside the donor cassette and within the 3' donor cassette (HindIII/XmaI) or within the 5' donor cassette and in intron 1 (NcoI/EcoRI) indicating precise single-copy donor integration.
evidence: This is directly observed in the Southern blot data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Transcript analysis in gfp-rx2 homozygous F3 embryos exclusively uncovered a single fusion gfp-rx2 transcript.
source: Furthermore, transcript analysis in gfp-rx2 homozygous F3 embryos exclusively uncovered a single fusion gfp-rx2 transcript (Figure 3C and C').
evidence: This is supported by RT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The simple 5'Biotin modification at both ends of long dsDNA donors by conventional PCR amplification provides the means to favor HDR without interfering with the cellular DNA repair machinery.
source: Taken together the simple 5'Biotin modification at both ends of long dsDNA donors by conventional PCR amplification presented here provides the means to favor HDR without interfering with the cellular DNA repair machinery.
evidence: This is the main conclusion drawn from all the experimental data presented in the study.

claim: For efficient recombination the quality of the modified primers, that is the fraction of primers actually labeled with biotin and therefore the quality of the 5' protected long ds DNA PCR product, is essential.
source: For efficient recombination the quality of the modified primers, that is the fraction of primers actually labeled with biotin and therefore the quality of the 5' protected long ds DNA PCR product, is essential.
evidence: This is inferred from the experimental observations and understanding of the mechanism.

claim: The integration of 5' modified PCR fragments larger than 2 kb does in principle not pose a problem.
source: The integration of 5' modified PCR fragments larger than 2 kb does in principle not pose a problem.
evidence: This is supported by the authors' experience with larger cassettes.

claim: Cassettes of up to 8.6 kb have been successfully integrated via HDR by in vivo linearization of the donor plasmid.
source: We already successfully integrated cassettes of up to 8.6 kb (data not shown) via HDR by in vivo linearization of the donor plasmid (Stemmer et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on unpublished data from the authors and a citation to Stemmer et al., 2015.

claim: The quality of the end-protected PCR product is likely to drop with higher length in part due to the (UV–) nicking in the extraction and purification process.
source: In the approach presented here, the quality of the end-protected PCR product is likely to drop with higher length in part due to the (UV–) nicking in the extraction and purification process.
evidence: This is speculation based on known properties of DNA handling.

claim: The PCR cycles used to probe for the successful single integration via HDR must not exceed a total of 30 to avoid misleading in vitro fusion-PCR artifacts.
source: Irrespective of the donor cassette size, the PCR cycles used to probe for the successful single integration via HDR must not exceed a total of 30 to avoid misleading in vitro fusion-PCR artifacts (own data and [Won and Dawid, 2017]).
evidence: This is based on the authors' own observations and a citation to Won and Dawid, 2017.

claim: There is no apparent G2 phase before mid-blastula-transition in amphibia (Xenopus) and fish (Danio rerio) with the marked exception of the first cleavage, where a G2 phase has been reported.
source: As reported extensively, there is no apparent G2 phase before mid-blastula-transition in amphibia (Xenopus) and fish (Danio rerio) with the marked exception of the first cleavage, where a G2 phase has been reported (Kimelman, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kimelman, 2014.

claim: The germline transmission rates obtained for the tagging of Rx1 and Rx2 indicated HDR events after the two-cell stage, predominantly at the 4-cell and subsequent stages.
source: The germline transmission rates obtained for the tagging of Rx1 and Rx2 indicated HDR events after the two-cell stage, predominantly at the 4-cell and subsequent stages.
evidence: This is inferred from the germline transmission data.

claim: The slower cycling of medaka compared to zebrafish results in an extension of the G2 phase in the first cell cycle by more than 150%.
source: The slower cycling of medaka compared to zebrafish results in an extension of the G2 phase in the first cell cycle by more than 150% (total cycle zebrafish: 45 min [Kimmel et al., 1995], medaka: 65 min [Iwamatsu, 2004]).
evidence: This is calculated from cited data on cell cycle timing in zebrafish and medaka.

claim: The total cell cycle in zebrafish is 45 min.
source: The slower cycling of medaka compared to zebrafish results in an extension of the G2 phase in the first cell cycle by more than 150% (total cycle zebrafish: 45 min [Kimmel et al., 1995], medaka: 65 min [Iwamatsu, 2004]).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kimmel et al., 1995.

claim: The total cell cycle in medaka is 65 min.
source: The slower cycling of medaka compared to zebrafish results in an extension of the G2 phase in the first cell cycle by more than 150% (total cycle zebrafish: 45 min [Kimmel et al., 1995], medaka: 65 min [Iwamatsu, 2004]).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Iwamatsu, 2004.

claim: Subsequent cell cycles in medaka are 40 min compared to 15 min in zebrafish.
source: This extended cell cycle length is in particular apparent also in the subsequent cycles in medaka (15 min zebrafish [Kimmel et al., 1995], 40 min medaka [Iwamatsu, 2004]).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Kimmel et al., 1995 and Iwamatsu, 2004.

claim: Phosphorylation of RNA polymerase, a prerequisite for the expression of the first zygotic transcripts, has been reported to start at the 64-cell stage in medaka.
source: Interestingly, phosphorylation of RNA polymerase, a prerequisite for the expression of the first zygotic transcripts has been reported to start at the 64cell stage in medaka (Kraeussling et al., 2011) and asynchronous divisions, a hallmark of MBT, are observed already at the transition of the 16- to 32-cell stage (Kraeussling et al., 2011), suggesting species-specific differences in the onset of zygotic transcription and consequently the lengthening of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kraeussling et al., 2011.

claim: Asynchronous divisions, a hallmark of MBT, are observed already at the transition of the 16- to 32-cell stage in medaka.
source: Interestingly, phosphorylation of RNA polymerase, a prerequisite for the expression of the first zygotic transcripts has been reported to start at the 64cell stage in medaka (Kraeussling et al., 2011) and asynchronous divisions, a hallmark of MBT, are observed already at the transition of the 16- to 32-cell stage (Kraeussling et al., 2011), suggesting species-specific differences in the onset of zygotic transcription and consequently the lengthening of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Kraeussling et al., 2011.

claim: There are species-specific differences in the onset of zygotic transcription and consequently the lengthening of the cell cycle.
source: Interestingly, phosphorylation of RNA polymerase, a prerequisite for the expression of the first zygotic transcripts has been reported to start at the 64cell stage in medaka (Kraeussling et al., 2011) and asynchronous divisions, a hallmark of MBT, are observed already at the transition of the 16- to 32-cell stage (Kraeussling et al., 2011), suggesting species-specific differences in the onset of zygotic transcription and consequently the lengthening of the cell cycle.
evidence: This is inferred from the cited observations about medaka development.

claim: The approach facilitates the highly efficient detection of HDR events by GFP tagging even in non-essential genes.
source: Our approach facilitates the highly efficient detection of HDR events by GFP tagging even in non-essential genes.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental results for rx2, rx1, and actb.

claim: The locus-specific expression of GFP is an excellent predictor for precise, single-copy HDR-mediated integration already in the injected generation.
source: Other than in non-modified dsDNA donors, the locus-specific expression of GFP is an excellent predictor for precise, single-copy HDR-mediated integration already in the injected generation.
evidence: This is supported by the high correlation between GFP expression and confirmed HDR events shown in the genotyping data.

claim: HDR rates in GFP positive embryos can be up to 60% in the injected generation.
source: This allows an easy selection and results in HDR rates in GFP positive embryos of up to 60% in the injected generation.
evidence: This is calculated from the experimental data for rx2.

claim: HDR rates can be even higher in essential loci, such as dnmt1, where the full functionality of the (modified) gene under investigation is required for the survival of the affected cells, tissues, organs or organisms.
source: This rate can even be higher in essential loci, such as dnmt1, where the full functionality of the (modified) gene under investigation is required for the survival of the affected cells, tissues, organs or organisms, thus providing the means for effective positive selection for single, fully functional integrates.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the 100% HDR rate in GFP-positive dnmt1 embryos.

claim: Approximately 400 bp flanking the insertion site in 5' and 3' direction are sufficient for HDR.
source: It is interesting to note that approximately 400 bp flanking the insertion site in 5' and 3' direction are sufficient for HDR.
evidence: This is observed from the successful HDR with homology flanks of approximately 400 bp used in the study.

claim: The use of modified universal primers for the two donor template vectors employed allowed a flexible application of the procedure and ensured a high quality of the PCR generated 5' modified long dsDNA donors.
source: The use of modified universal primers for the two donor template vectors employed allowed a flexible application of the procedure and ensured a high quality of the PCR generated 5' modified long dsDNA donors.
evidence: This is based on the successful application of the method across multiple loci.

claim: The primer-introduced non-homology regions in the very periphery of the long dsDNA donors did not negatively impact on the HDR efficiency.
source: Strikingly, the primer-introduced non-homology regions in the very periphery of the long dsDNA donors did not negatively impact on the HDR efficiency.
evidence: This is observed from the high HDR efficiency despite the presence of vector backbone sequences.

claim: The simplicity and high reproducibility of the proof-of-concept analysis highlight that the presented protection of both 5' ends of long dsDNA donors prevent multimerization and promote precise insertion/replacement of DNA elements.
source: Taken together, the simplicity and high reproducibility of our proof-of-concept analysis highlight that the presented protection of both 5' ends of long dsDNA donors prevent multimerization and promote precise insertion/replacement of DNA elements, thus facilitating functional studies in basic research as well as therapeutic interventions.
evidence: This is the overall conclusion drawn from all experimental results.

claim: The presented approach facilitates functional studies in basic research as well as therapeutic interventions.
source: Taken together, the simplicity and high reproducibility of our proof-of-concept analysis highlight that the presented protection of both 5' ends of long dsDNA donors prevent multimerization and promote precise insertion/replacement of DNA elements, thus facilitating functional studies in basic research as well as therapeutic interventions.
evidence: This is speculation about the potential applications of the method.
